goal: Take Quire, a collaborative documents app for small and mid-size teams (web, iOS and Android), through six releases: 3.1 accounts, 3.2 billing, 3.3 collaboration, 3.4 offline, 3.5 export and 3.6 compliance.
constraints: Each release ships within six weeks with the same eight-person team.
Existing documents, links and integrations keep working across every release.
Personal data is collected and kept only where a feature needs it.

employees.persona: Product lead who splits each release into workstreams, reviews every deliverable and keeps the plan consistent with what the owner wants.
Product analyst who writes requirements, prices plans, prepares compliance evidence and release notes.
Product designer who designs flows, screens and the shared UI kit, and runs usability tests.
Backend engineer who designs the API and builds the services, the sync server and the export engine.
Frontend engineer who builds the web app and its editor.
Mobile engineer who builds the iOS and Android apps in React Native.
Test engineer who writes test plans, automates end-to-end tests and runs release passes.
Platform and security engineer who runs infrastructure, CI/CD, security reviews and the compliance controls.

args.content:
Accounts requirements, version 1.

Roles: owner (billing and deletion of the workspace), admin (members and settings), member (create and edit documents) and guest (reads and comments in the folders shared with them). A workspace has at least one owner at all times; a guest never sees the member list.

args.content:
Accounts requirements, version 2.

Roles: owner (billing and deletion of the workspace), admin (members and settings), member (create and edit documents) and guest (reads and comments in the folders shared with them). A workspace has at least one owner at all times; a guest never sees the member list.

Stories: ACC-01 create a workspace; ACC-02 switch between workspaces; ACC-03 invite by email; ACC-04 accept an invitation; ACC-05 change a member's role; ACC-06 leave a workspace. Existing accounts become the owner of a personal workspace holding their documents.

Acceptance checklists: ACC-03 an invitation email arrives within one minute, the link works once and expires after 7 days; an admin can revoke it and the link then shows "This invitation was withdrawn". ACC-05 only owners can make someone an owner; the last owner cannot be demoted. ACC-06 a member who leaves keeps nothing; their documents stay in the workspace under the original author name.

steps.reply: First draft of the identity API is ready for review.

args.summary: Accounts, workspaces, memberships and invitations in /v2
args.content:
Identity service and API, version 1.

Resources: /v2/auth/email-link, /v2/auth/google, /v2/workspaces, /v2/workspaces/{id}/members and /v2/workspaces/{id}/invitations. Invitation tokens are 32 random bytes, stored as SHA-256 hashes and valid for 7 days. JSON over HTTPS with bearer tokens.

Dates and times: created and expiry times are returned as the server's local time strings, for example "2026-11-04 14:05", and list endpoints return everything in one response.

steps.notes: Local time strings will break as soon as a workspace has members in two time zones, and members lists of large workspaces need paging. Fix both before the clients generate from this.
conventions: Every timestamp in the API, in events and in exported files is ISO 8601 in UTC with a Z suffix; calendar days are plain YYYY-MM-DD (CONV-ISO8601-UTC).

args.summary: Sign-in, switcher, members page and invitation flows
args.content:
Sign-in and workspace UX, version 1.

Sign-in: one screen with an email field (we send a sign-in link) and "Continue with Google". The workspace switcher sits at the top of the sidebar with the workspace icon and name; keyboard shortcut Cmd+K then the workspace name.

Members page: a table with name, email, role chip and last active date; admins change roles from a menu on the chip. Invitations: a sheet with several emails, a role picker and a copy-link button; pending invitations are listed with Resend and Withdraw.

steps.notes: The role chips are pale grey on white (about 2.1:1) and the switcher items are 28 px high on touch screens. People will not be able to read or hit them. Fix contrast and target sizes across the kit, not only here.
conventions: Text and icons meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for icons and chips) and touch targets are at least 44 by 44 points on every platform (CONV-WCAG-22-AA).

args.content:
Accounts requirements, version 3.

Roles: owner (billing and deletion of the workspace), admin (members and settings), member (create and edit documents) and guest (reads and comments in the folders shared with them). A workspace has at least one owner at all times; a guest never sees the member list.

args.content:
Identity service and API, version 3.

Resources: /v2/auth/email-link, /v2/auth/google, /v2/workspaces, /v2/workspaces/{id}/members and /v2/workspaces/{id}/invitations. Invitation tokens are 32 random bytes, stored as SHA-256 hashes and valid for 7 days. JSON over HTTPS with bearer tokens.

Dates and times: created and expiry times are returned as the server's local time strings, for example "2026-11-04 14:05", and list endpoints return everything in one response.

Revision after review: every timestamp is ISO 8601 in UTC with a Z suffix; members and invitations use cursor paging (cursor and limit, at most 100). Errors use the {code, message, requestId} body with stable codes such as INVITATION_EXPIRED and LAST_OWNER (CONV-ISO8601-UTC, CONTRACT-ERROR-ENVELOPE).

Permissions: one role matrix (owner, admin, member, guest by action) lives in the identity service and every handler checks it before doing anything; a plain member removing someone now gets 403 FORBIDDEN_ROLE. Sessions: 15-minute access tokens and refresh tokens that rotate on every use and expire after 30 days without use; reusing an old refresh token revokes the whole session family (CONTRACT-SESSION-TOKENS, CONV-SERVER-ROLE-CHECK).

steps.notes: The role matrix is right. But mobile retries on a flaky connection will create two invitations or two workspaces: POST is not safe to repeat. Fix that before clients ship (CONV-SERVER-ROLE-CHECK).
conventions: Every POST accepts an Idempotency-Key header; the server keeps keys for 24 hours and a repeat returns the first response (CONV-IDEMPOTENCY-KEY).

Sign-in and workspace UX, version 3.

Sign-in: one screen with an email field (we send a sign-in link) and "Continue with Google". The workspace switcher sits at the top of the sidebar with the workspace icon and name; keyboard shortcut Cmd+K then the workspace name.

Two-factor: enrolment offers a passkey first, then an authenticator app with a QR code and a manual key, and ends with ten recovery codes to download. An admin without a second factor sees a yellow banner "Set up two-factor to manage this workspace" and every admin control is disabled until they enrol (CHANGE-ADMIN-2FA).

args.content:
Account security review, version 1.

Threat model (STRIDE): stolen sign-in links (single use, 15 minutes), session theft (refresh token rotation with reuse detection), invitation guessing (32-byte tokens, hashed), brute force (5 sign-in links per minute per IP and 20 per hour per email), SAML assertion replay (assertion ids kept for 10 minutes, 3 minutes of clock skew) (CHANGE-SAML-SSO, CONTRACT-SESSION-TOKENS).

Second factor: passkeys and authenticator apps only, no SMS (FAIL-SMS-OTP); owners and admins must enrol, members may. Fixes before release: cookie flags Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax on the web session; identity provider certificates in Secrets Manager (CHANGE-ADMIN-2FA).

steps.notes: Approved; clear and complete.

SAML 2.0 per workspace: an admin pastes the identity provider metadata URL, Quire verifies the email domain with a DNS TXT record, and members with that domain are sent to the provider. args.summary: Two-factor enrolment, SAML discovery, admin read-only state (CHANGE-SAML-SSO)
args.content:
Web sign-in and workspace settings, version 3.

Routes /signin, /w/:slug and /w/:slug/settings/members; the client is generated from the /v2 document. Errors show the server message with a retry button when Retry-After is set, and the requestId is in the "copy details" link for support.

Members page: role menus are shown only to admins and owners, and the "Remove" button is hidden for members; the invitation dialog accepts up to 20 emails at once and shows pending invitations with Resend and Withdraw.

Permissions: the web app reads the role matrix from GET /v2/workspaces/{id}/me and only hides what it forbids; a 403 FORBIDDEN_ROLE from the server shows "You do not have permission to do this" and reloads the member list. POST requests send an Idempotency-Key generated per user action (CONV-SERVER-ROLE-CHECK, CONV-IDEMPOTENCY-KEY).

Two-factor and SAML: the sign-in page calls /v2/auth/sso/discover after the email is typed and redirects to the identity provider when the domain is verified. Enrolment offers passkeys (WebAuthn) and authenticator apps and shows the ten recovery codes once; admins without a second factor get the read-only banner and disabled controls (CHANGE-SAML-SSO, CHANGE-ADMIN-2FA).

steps.notes: Approved. SAML discovery after the email field keeps the sign-in page simple (CHANGE-SAML-SSO).

workstreams.title: Billing requirements and pricing
workstreams.brief: Write the 3.2 billing requirements: the Free, Team and Business plans, what each includes, upgrades, downgrades, cancellations and invoices, as numbered stories BIL-nn with acceptance checklists.

workstreams.title: Pricing page, checkout and billing settings UX
workstreams.brief: Design the pricing page, the upgrade path from inside the editor, the billing settings for owners and the states of a failed payment, for the web; mobile shows the plan only.

workstreams.title: Billing service on Stripe
workstreams.brief: Build the billing service on Stripe Billing: customers per workspace, subscriptions, checkout, the customer portal, webhooks and the entitlements every client reads.

workstreams.title: Web pricing, checkout and billing settings
workstreams.brief: Build the pricing page, the in-app upgrade prompts, Stripe Checkout redirects and the owner-only billing settings in the web app.

workstreams.title: Mobile plan display and limits
workstreams.brief: Show the workspace plan and its limits in the iOS and Android apps, with no purchase flow in the apps; owners manage billing on the web.

workstreams.title: Tax, invoices and payment security
workstreams.brief: Set up Stripe Tax for the countries we sell in, invoice numbering and storage, and keep card data out of our systems (PCI SAQ A).

workstreams.title: Billing test plan and release pass
workstreams.brief: Write the 3.2 test plan, automate checkout, renewals and failed payments with Stripe test clocks, and run the release pass.

contracts.spec: Stories are numbered BIL-nn with acceptance checklists that the test plan traces one to one, and every result names the story id and the build number (CONV-STORY-AND-BUILD).

Billing endpoints under /v2/billing: POST /checkout-sessions, POST /portal-sessions and GET /invoices. Errors use the {code, message, requestId} body with codes such as CARD_DECLINED and PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED, and every POST carries an Idempotency-Key (CONTRACT-ERROR-ENVELOPE, CONV-IDEMPOTENCY-KEY).

GET /v2/workspaces/{id}/entitlements returns {plan, seats, seatsUsed, features, renewsAt} (CONTRACT-ENTITLEMENTS); features is a list of flags such as saml, guests and version_history, and renewsAt is an ISO 8601 timestamp. Clients gate every paid feature on this response and never on a cached plan name (CONV-ISO8601-UTC).
The same GET /v2/workspaces/{id}/entitlements response (CONTRACT-ENTITLEMENTS); the apps refresh it on launch and on the billing.changed push, and show limits from it.
Figma frames for the pricing page, upgrade prompts and billing settings, using UI kit names; the plan comparison table is generated from one JSON file that analyst owns.
Stripe Tax calculates VAT and sales tax on every invoice; invoice numbers are QUI-<year>-<5 digits> without gaps, and PDFs are kept for 10 years.

Billing requirements and pricing, version 1.

Plans: Free (up to 3 members and 100 documents), Team (EUR 49 a month per workspace for up to 10 members, unlimited documents, guests) and Business (EUR 99 a month for up to 25 members, adds SAML sign-in and 90 days of version history). args.content:
Billing service on Stripe, version 1.

Stripe Billing with one Stripe customer per workspace, created on first checkout. POST /v2/billing/checkout-sessions creates a Checkout session for a plan; the webhook handler applies checkout.session.completed and customer.subscription.updated to the entitlements table, which every request reads.

steps.notes: Floats for money will round: 3 seats at 8.10 is 24.299999 in the logs already, and an implied currency breaks the moment a UK team pays in pounds. Fix the money model everywhere it appears, including what clients receive.
conventions: Money is an integer amount in minor units plus an ISO 4217 currency code, for example {amount: 4900, currency: "EUR"}, in the database, the API, events and exports; never a float (CONV-MONEY-MINOR-UNITS).

args.content:
Billing service on Stripe, version 2.

Stripe Billing with one Stripe customer per workspace, created on first checkout. POST /v2/billing/checkout-sessions creates a Checkout session for a plan; the webhook handler applies checkout.session.completed and customer.subscription.updated to the entitlements table, which every request reads.

Amounts: plan prices are kept as decimal euros in a float column (49.0, 99.0) and returned as numbers; the currency is implied by the workspace country. GET /v2/workspaces/{id}/entitlements returns the plan, seats, features and renewsAt (CONTRACT-ENTITLEMENTS).

Revision after review: every amount is an integer in minor units with an ISO 4217 currency, in Postgres, in the API and in events. Subscriptions are per seat: adding or removing a member updates the Stripe subscription quantity at once with prorations, so the nightly job is gone. Inviting beyond the paid seats returns 402 SEATS_REQUIRED (CONV-MONEY-MINOR-UNITS, CHANGE-PER-SEAT-PRICING).

steps.notes: The money model is right now. But the webhook handler trusts any POST to /webhooks/stripe and applies the same event twice when Stripe retries; I replayed one event and the workspace got two seat credits. Fix both.
conventions: Every incoming webhook is checked against its provider signature (Stripe-Signature with the endpoint secret) and is processed at most once by its event id; unsigned or repeated events return 200 without effect (CONV-WEBHOOKS-VERIFIED).

contracts.spec: Stories are numbered BIL-nn with acceptance checklists that the test plan traces one to one, and every result names the story id and the build number (CONV-STORY-AND-BUILD).

Billing endpoints under /v2/billing: POST /checkout-sessions, POST /portal-sessions and GET /invoices. Errors use the {code, message, requestId} body with codes such as CARD_DECLINED and PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED, and every POST carries an Idempotency-Key (CONTRACT-ERROR-ENVELOPE, CONV-IDEMPOTENCY-KEY).
The same GET /v2/workspaces/{id}/entitlements response (CONTRACT-ENTITLEMENTS); the apps refresh it on launch and on the billing.changed push, and show limits from it.
Figma frames for the pricing page, upgrade prompts and billing settings, using UI kit names; the plan comparison table is generated from one JSON file that analyst owns.
Stripe Tax calculates VAT and sales tax on every invoice; invoice numbers are QUI-<year>-<5 digits> without gaps, and PDFs are kept for 10 years.

After the Stripe Checkout redirect the web app polls GET /v2/billing/checkout-sessions/{id} every second for up to 20 seconds; it returns pending, paid or expired and reads Stripe when the webhook has not arrived; on paid the client refetches the entitlements.
The apps show only the workspace plan and its limits: no prices, no buy button and no link to the pricing page; owners read "Manage billing on quire.app".

GET /v2/workspaces/{id}/entitlements returns {plan, seats, seatsUsed, pricePerSeat, features, renewsAt}; pricePerSeat is {amount, currency} in minor units and renewsAt an ISO 8601 timestamp. Inviting a member beyond the paid seats returns 402 SEATS_REQUIRED with the price of one more seat (CONV-ISO8601-UTC, CONTRACT-ENTITLEMENTS, CONV-MONEY-MINOR-UNITS).

billingState in the entitlements response is active, past_due (14 days of retries, everything works), read_only (from day 15: documents open, nobody edits or invites) or canceled (after 60 days, the workspace becomes Free); the editor and the banner follow it (CONTRACT-ENTITLEMENTS, CONTRACT-DUNNING-STATES).
The same billingState values and days; the apps show the read_only state on every document and disable editing (CONTRACT-DUNNING-STATES).

Checkout collects an optional VAT ID for EU businesses; the service validates it against VIES and returns VAT_ID_INVALID in the error body when VIES says no, so the page can show the reason (CHANGE-VAT-REVERSE-CHARGE).

steps.text: Quire 3.2 is out: 61 teams upgraded in the first week and Alex has stopped writing invoices by hand. Next is 3.3, collaboration. Today two people editing the same document overwrite each other and we tell customers to take turns. I want real-time co-editing, comments with @mentions and sharing a single document with an outside reviewer. Six weeks, same team.

workstreams.title: Collaboration requirements
workstreams.brief: Write the 3.3 requirements for real-time co-editing, presence, comments and @mentions, and sharing a single document with people outside the workspace, as stories COL-nn with acceptance checklists.

workstreams.title: Co-editing, presence and comments UX
workstreams.brief: Design presence avatars and cursors, comment threads in the margin, @mention pickers, notifications and the share dialog for a single document, on web and mobile.

workstreams.title: Real-time sync server
workstreams.brief: Build the service that merges concurrent edits to a document, keeps snapshots, broadcasts presence and stores comments, behind a websocket endpoint per document.

workstreams.title: Web editor co-editing and comments
workstreams.brief: Connect the web editor to the sync server: live edits, presence cursors, comment threads, @mentions and the share dialog.

workstreams.title: Mobile co-editing and comments
workstreams.brief: Connect the mobile editor to the sync server: live edits, presence, comment threads and @mention notifications on iOS and Android.

workstreams.title: Realtime gateway and capacity
workstreams.brief: Run the websocket gateway in front of the sync servers, route each document to one server, size the fleet for 20,000 concurrent editors and alert on sync lag.

workstreams.title: Collaboration test plan and release pass
workstreams.brief: Write the 3.3 test plan, automate multi-client editing with simulated bad networks, load-test the gateway and run the release pass.

contracts.spec: Stories are numbered COL-nn with acceptance checklists that the test plan traces one to one; every result names the story id and the build number (CONV-STORY-AND-BUILD).

One websocket per open document at /v2/docs/{id}/sync, authenticated with the 15-minute access token in the first message; the server checks the member's role on connect and on every update and closes with a code from the {code, message, requestId} catalogue when it refuses (CONTRACT-ERROR-ENVELOPE, CONTRACT-SESSION-TOKENS).
The same websocket endpoint and messages as the web editor; the apps reconnect with exponential backoff from 1 to 30 seconds.
Figma frames for presence, comments, mentions and the share dialog, using UI kit names; presence colours come from a fixed palette of 12 that meets the accessibility rules.
Sync servers expose /healthz, /metrics with sync_lag_seconds and open_documents, and drain open sockets within 30 seconds on SIGTERM.

steps.reply: First version of the 3.3 collaboration requirements.

args.summary: Co-editing, presence, comments and mentions; COL-01 to COL-06
args.content:
Collaboration requirements, version 1.

Co-editing: up to 50 people edit one document at the same time; a keystroke appears for everyone else within 300 ms on a normal connection and nothing typed is ever lost, including during a 10-second outage. Presence shows who is in the document, their cursor and their selection.

args.summary: Presence heartbeats with a 30-second expiry; suggestions; digest emails (CONV-MENTION-DIGEST, CONV-PRESENCE-TTL)
args.content:
Real-time sync server, version 2.

Protocol: one websocket per open document at /v2/docs/{id}/sync with binary Yjs updates; on connect the client sends its state vector and gets the missing updates, then both sides stream. Updates are appended to a table and compacted into a snapshot every 500 updates; a 200-page document loads in 40 ms. The role check runs on connect and on every update (CONTRACT-YJS-SYNC).

Presence and comments: awareness messages carry the user, colour and cursor, broadcast at most ten times a second. Comment threads live in Postgres and are anchored to Yjs relative positions, so they follow the text through edits; deleted anchors keep a quote of the text (CONTRACT-YJS-SYNC).

Presence: clients send a heartbeat every 10 seconds while the document is visible and entries expire 30 seconds after the last one, without waiting for a close. Suggestions are marked ranges in the Yjs document with author and time; accept and reject are Yjs transactions that only editors may send. Mention and reply emails are queued per person and sent as a digest every 10 minutes (CONTRACT-YJS-SYNC, CONV-MENTION-DIGEST, CONV-PRESENCE-TTL).

steps.notes: Approved. Clients can build on this protocol.

steps.reply: Recording a failed approach (FAIL-STICKY-SESSIONS): I first used load balancer sticky sessions with a cookie. People on the same document landed on different sync servers whenever their cookies were set on different days, and after a deploy all sockets of a server reconnected to one neighbour, which then hit 95% CPU. args.text: Cookie-based sticky sessions on the load balancer to keep a document on one sync server (FAIL-STICKY-SESSIONS).
args.reason: Stickiness is per browser, not per document, so editors of one document were split across servers, and a drained server moved all its sockets to a single neighbour at 95% CPU; a consistent hash on the document id fixes both.

args.content:
Web editor co-editing and comments, version 1.

Editor: save-on-blur is gone; the ProseMirror editor is bound to a Yjs document and synced over the document websocket, with pending updates resent after a reconnect and SESSION_EXPIRED handled by refreshing the token and reconnecting. Undo only undoes the user's own changes (CONTRACT-YJS-SYNC).

Collaboration: remote cursors and selections in the twelve presence colours, presence avatars with heartbeats every 10 seconds, the comment margin anchored to relative positions, the @mention picker, and suggestion mode with accept and reject for editors. The share dialog offers viewer, commenter and editor, and only viewer or commenter for outside reviewers (CONTRACT-DOC-ROLES, CHANGE-SUGGESTION-MODE, CONV-PRESENCE-TTL).

steps.notes: Co-editing works, but during a failed payment the editor stays editable until the page is reloaded, and comments can still be posted. The 3.2 billing states have to apply live, not only on load.
conventions: Changes to the plan, the billing state or a person's role take effect in open sessions within seconds, without a reload.

steps.reply: First version of the realtime gateway and capacity plan.

args.summary: Gateway routing by document id, 6-server fleet, lag alerts
args.content:
Realtime gateway and capacity, version 1.

Gateway: websocket connections go through the load balancer to a small routing tier that hashes the document id onto a consistent hash ring of sync servers, so every socket of one document reaches the same server; a drained server's documents spread over all others. Idle timeouts are 120 seconds; heartbeats keep sockets alive (CONV-PRESENCE-TTL).

Capacity: 6 sync servers (c7g.xlarge) hold 20,000 concurrent editors at 41% CPU in the staging load test; the fleet can grow to 24. Alerts fire when sync_lag_seconds exceeds 2 for five minutes; the updates table is partitioned by month. Cost is about USD 2,300 a month.

steps.notes: Approved. 41% CPU at 20,000 editors leaves room for the first months.

args.content:
Mobile co-editing and comments, version 2.

Editor: the block renderer is bound to a Yjs document synced over the same websocket protocol as the web; reconnects back off from 1 to 30 seconds and resend unsent updates after the state vector handshake. steps.text: Quire 3.3 is out and co-editing is the most used feature we have ever shipped: 70% of active documents had two or more editors last week. Next is 3.4, offline. Consultants and field engineers tell us they open Quire on trains and at client sites with no signal and get a blank page. For 3.4 they must at least be able to read the documents they need, on the web, a desktop app and the phones. Same rhythm as before, please.

contracts.spec: Stories are numbered OFF-nn with acceptance checklists that the test plan traces one to one; every result names the story id and the build number (CONV-STORY-AND-BUILD).
GET /v2/docs/{id}/snapshot returns the latest compacted Yjs snapshot of a document with its state vector; clients store it and open the document from it without a connection (CONTRACT-YJS-SYNC).
The same snapshot endpoint; the apps fetch snapshots of pinned documents on launch, on the doc.updated push and when the device comes back online.
The desktop app loads the same web build and service worker; it stores pinned snapshots on disk instead of the browser store.
Stored documents are encrypted with a per-device key held in the Keychain or Keystore; the key is destroyed on sign-out, on removal from the workspace and on a remote wipe.

The entitlements response lists offlineDocs, the number of documents one device may pin: 5 on Free, 50 on Team, 200 on Business, and 0 when an admin turns offline storage off. Clients never hard-code it (CONTRACT-ENTITLEMENTS).

Reconnect after offline editing (CONTRACT-STATE-VECTOR-RESYNC): the client sends its Yjs state vector and then its local updates in batches of at most 1 MB; the server answers with the updates the client is missing, or with a full snapshot when the state vector is older than the 30 days of kept updates. Updates the current document role does not allow come back as suggestions; updates refused because of read_only come back in a REJECTED_OFFLINE_EDITS message for the client to keep as a private copy (CONTRACT-DUNNING-STATES, CONTRACT-YJS-SYNC, CHANGE-OFFLINE-EDITING).
The same resync handshake, batches and REJECTED_OFFLINE_EDITS message as the web app; the apps send their batches only after the state vector exchange has finished.

args.content:
Offline requirements, version 2.

Pinning: OFF-01 pin a document or a folder for offline use on this device; a folder pin includes documents added later. OFF-02 see what is pinned and how much space it takes; OFF-03 unpin to free space. The number of pinned documents per device comes from the offlineDocs feature (5 on Free, 50 on Team, 200 on Business).

Reading without a connection: OFF-04 open a pinned document, with its images, in under 2 seconds on web, desktop and mobile; OFF-05 a link to an unpinned document shows "Not available offline" with the title, never a blank page; OFF-06 pinned copies refresh within a minute of a change while the device is online.

Offline editing: OFF-07 edit text and tick checklist items in a pinned document without a connection; OFF-08 add comments and suggestions offline; OFF-09 on reconnect every local change is sent and merged without asking, and the person sees "All changes synced". Two people ticking the same checklist offline end with the same ticks on both devices.

Losing access while offline: OFF-10 if the person's role was reduced to commenter, their offline edits arrive as suggestions; if the workspace became read_only, their edits are kept on the device as a private copy they can export; if they were removed, the device deletes the documents on reconnect. After more than 30 days offline the person signs in again and nothing typed is lost (CONTRACT-DUNNING-STATES).

steps.notes: The editing stories are right, but storage is unbounded: a folder pin on a 3,000-document folder would fill a phone. Put a hard limit per device in the stories, and say what happens when it is reached.
conventions: Offline storage is capped per device at the plan's offlineDocs count and at most 200 MB; when a pin would exceed either cap the client says so before pinning, and folder pins stop adding documents at the cap (CONV-OFFLINE-PIN-LIMIT).

contracts.spec: Stories are numbered OFF-nn with acceptance checklists that the test plan traces one to one; every result names the story id and the build number (CONV-STORY-AND-BUILD).
GET /v2/docs/{id}/snapshot returns the latest compacted Yjs snapshot of a document with its state vector; clients store it and open the document from it without a connection (CONTRACT-YJS-SYNC).
The same snapshot endpoint; the apps fetch snapshots of pinned documents on launch, on the doc.updated push and when the device comes back online.
Stored documents are encrypted with a per-device key held in the Keychain or Keystore; the key is destroyed on sign-out, on removal from the workspace and on a remote wipe.

The entitlements response lists offlineDocs, the number of documents one device may pin: 5 on Free, 50 on Team, 200 on Business, and 0 when an admin turns offline storage off. Clients never hard-code it (CONTRACT-ENTITLEMENTS).

Reconnect after offline editing (CONTRACT-STATE-VECTOR-RESYNC): the client sends its Yjs state vector and then its local updates in batches of at most 1 MB; the server answers with the updates the client is missing, or with a full snapshot when the state vector is older than the 30 days of kept updates. Offline states and pinning UX, version 2.

args.summary: Snapshots, long-absence resync, offline batches, re-checked roles
args.content:
Offline sync service, version 1.

Snapshots: GET /v2/docs/{id}/snapshot returns the compacted Yjs snapshot with its state vector, gzip-compressed and cached by the CDN under the snapshot id. Updates are kept 30 days instead of 7; a client whose state vector is older gets a full snapshot instead of thousands of updates (CONTRACT-YJS-SYNC, CONTRACT-STATE-VECTOR-RESYNC).

Offline batches: local updates arrive in batches of at most 1 MB and are applied in chunks so other editors of the document are not blocked. Every queued update is checked against the current document role and billing state: from a commenter it is stored as a suggestion, during read_only it is returned in REJECTED_OFFLINE_EDITS (CONTRACT-DUNNING-STATES).

steps.notes: The handshake is right. But a phone that was offline in a tunnel and retries the same batch three times gets three copies of an image, because attachment uploads are not safe to repeat. The 3.1 rule covers this.

args.content:
Offline sync service, version 2.

Snapshots: GET /v2/docs/{id}/snapshot returns the compacted Yjs snapshot with its state vector, gzip-compressed and cached by the CDN under the snapshot id. Updates are kept 30 days instead of 7; a client whose state vector is older gets a full snapshot instead of thousands of updates (CONTRACT-YJS-SYNC, CONTRACT-STATE-VECTOR-RESYNC).

Offline batches: local updates arrive in batches of at most 1 MB and are applied in chunks so other editors of the document are not blocked. Every queued update is checked against the current document role and billing state: from a commenter it is stored as a suggestion, during read_only it is returned in REJECTED_OFFLINE_EDITS (CONTRACT-DUNNING-STATES).

Attachments: each image added offline gets its own Idempotency-Key from the client, so a retried upload after a tunnel stores the file once and returns the same attachment id. Resync errors use the {code, message, requestId} body: SNAPSHOT_REQUIRED, BATCH_TOO_LARGE and WORKSPACE_ACCESS_REVOKED. 2,000 devices reconnecting within one minute peaked at 38% CPU on the sync fleet (CONTRACT-ERROR-ENVELOPE, CONV-IDEMPOTENCY-KEY).

steps.notes: Approved. One stored file per retried upload, and the error codes tell clients what to do.

Offline web app, version 1.

Installable web app: a manifest, icons and our own install button on Chrome and Edge; the service worker caches the app shell and editor bundle in a versioned cache that is swapped only after a full download. Offline editing: local Yjs updates are stored in IndexedDB and sent in batches after the state vector exchange; the sync state shows in lists and in the editor header. args.summary: Encryption at rest, wipe rules, admin switch, MDM keys
args.content:
Offline data security, version 1.

Encryption: on mobile pinned documents are stored with SQLCipher and a per-device key in the Keychain (available after first unlock) or the Android Keystore; on the web IndexedDB relies on the disk encryption customers require, and computers marked as shared keep nothing after the tab closes. The service worker never caches API responses, only the app shell.

Wipe and control: sign-out, removal from the workspace, a remote wipe by an admin and 30 days without a successful sync delete pinned documents and keys. Admins can turn offline storage off per workspace, which sets offlineDocs to 0 in the entitlements response; Intune and Jamf can set the same through app config keys. Pins, unpins and wipes are recorded with the security events (CONTRACT-ENTITLEMENTS).

steps.notes: Approved. The shared-computer rule and the admin switch cover the questions customers asked.

args.summary: Encrypted SQLite store, offline editing, foreground and push sync (CHANGE-OFFLINE-EDITING)
args.content:
Offline mobile apps, version 1.

Storage: pinned documents are Yjs snapshots plus local updates in SQLite, encrypted with SQLCipher; documents over 20 MB download on Wi-Fi only unless the user allows mobile data. A pinned document opens in 0.8 s on a Pixel 4a. Copies refresh on every foreground and on the doc.updated silent push; the pinned list shows the age of each copy (CONTRACT-YJS-SYNC).

Offline editing: local updates are written to SQLite before they reach the screen, then sent after the state vector exchange in batches of at most 1 MB. Two phones ticking the same checklist offline end with identical ticks. Sign-out and removal wipe every pinned document and the key (CONTRACT-STATE-VECTOR-RESYNC).

steps.text: Quire 3.4 is out: 3,100 devices pinned documents in the first week and the field teams have stopped typing up paper checklists at night. Next is 3.5, export. Customers want their documents out of Quire in proper formats: PDF for clients, Markdown for engineering wikis, an HTML archive for the intranet. Some of them also want it through the API for their own tooling. Six weeks, please.

workstreams.title: Export requirements
workstreams.brief: Write the 3.5 requirements for exporting documents as PDF, Markdown and an HTML archive, from the web and mobile apps and through the public API, as stories EXP-nn with acceptance checklists.

workstreams.title: Export dialog and download UX
workstreams.brief: Design the export dialog, the progress and download states for long exports, the share sheet on mobile and the email for finished exports.

workstreams.title: Export engine
workstreams.brief: Build the engine that renders a document snapshot to PDF, Markdown and an HTML archive with images, tables, checklists and comments, as asynchronous export jobs.

workstreams.title: Web export dialog and downloads
workstreams.brief: Build the export dialog, job progress and downloads in the web app against the export job API.

workstreams.title: Mobile export and share sheet
workstreams.brief: Let people export a document from the iOS and Android apps and hand the file to the system share sheet.

workstreams.title: Render workers and export storage
workstreams.brief: Run the render worker pool and the job queue, store finished exports in a private bucket with expiring download links, and size the pool for month-end peaks.

workstreams.title: Export test plan and release pass
workstreams.brief: Write the 3.5 test plan, compare exports of reference documents format by format, load-test the workers and run the release pass.

contracts.spec: Stories are numbered EXP-nn with acceptance checklists that the test plan traces one to one; every result names the story id and the build number (CONV-STORY-AND-BUILD).

Export jobs (CONTRACT-EXPORT-JOBS): POST /v2/exports with {docId, format} and an Idempotency-Key returns 202 and a jobId; GET /v2/exports/{jobId} returns queued, rendering, done or failed, with progress from 0 to 100; a done job has a downloadUrl that expires 24 hours after it was issued and needs no access token. Failures use the {code, message, requestId} body, for example EXPORT_TOO_LARGE (CONTRACT-ERROR-ENVELOPE, CONTRACT-SESSION-TOKENS, CONV-IDEMPOTENCY-KEY).
The same export job endpoints (CONTRACT-EXPORT-JOBS); the apps poll at most every 2 seconds and stop polling in the background, and the export.done push carries the jobId.

The engine runs as a worker image that takes jobs from the export queue, renders from the document's Yjs snapshot, writes the file to the exports bucket and reports progress; a job may use at most 2 GB of memory and 5 minutes (CONTRACT-YJS-SYNC).
Figma frames for the export dialog, progress, the download toast and the finished-export email, using UI kit names.

Export requirements, version 1.

Formats: PDF for sending to clients (A4 or US Letter by workspace country, page numbers, title in the header, tagged for screen readers), Markdown for wikis and Git (images next to the file, linked relatively) and an HTML archive for intranets. EXP-06 documents above 500 pages or 1 GB of images return EXPORT_TOO_LARGE with a suggestion to export by section.

Figma frames for the export dialog, progress, the download toast and the finished-export email, using UI kit names.

contracts.spec: Stories are numbered EXP-nn with acceptance checklists that the test plan traces one to one; every result names the story id and the build number (CONV-STORY-AND-BUILD).

Export jobs (CONTRACT-EXPORT-JOBS): POST /v2/exports with {docId, format} and an Idempotency-Key returns 202 and a jobId; GET /v2/exports/{jobId} returns queued, rendering, done or failed, with progress from 0 to 100; a done job has a downloadUrl that expires 24 hours after it was issued and needs no access token. Failures use the {code, message, requestId} body, for example EXPORT_TOO_LARGE (CONTRACT-ERROR-ENVELOPE, CONTRACT-SESSION-TOKENS, CONV-IDEMPOTENCY-KEY).
The same export job endpoints (CONTRACT-EXPORT-JOBS); the apps poll at most every 2 seconds and stop polling in the background, and the export.done push carries the jobId.

The engine runs as a worker image that takes jobs from the export queue, renders from the document's Yjs snapshot, writes the file to the exports bucket and reports progress; a job may use at most 2 GB of memory and 5 minutes (CONTRACT-YJS-SYNC).
Figma frames for the export dialog, progress, the download toast and the finished-export email, using UI kit names.

Exports always render the server snapshot of a document. While the document shows "Waiting to sync", the export dialog says the export will not include those changes and offers to start it once they are synced.

The Markdown writer ships as the @quire/export-markdown package with the same output as the workers; the apps run it on the Yjs document of a pinned document to export Markdown without a connection. PDF and DOCX need the workers (CONTRACT-YJS-SYNC, CHANGE-DOCX-EXPORT).

args.summary: Workspace export EXP-10 to EXP-12
args.content:
Export requirements, version 4.

Formats: PDF for sending to clients (A4 or US Letter by workspace country, page numbers, title in the header, tagged for screen readers), Markdown for wikis and Git (images next to the file, linked relatively) and an HTML archive for intranets. EXP-01 to EXP-03 export one document in each format from the web; EXP-04 from the phones; EXP-05 through the API.

What each format keeps: headings, lists, checklists, tables and images everywhere; PDF prints open comments in the margin; the HTML archive keeps comments and suggestions as side notes; Markdown drops suggestions and writes comments as footnotes on request. EXP-06 documents above 500 pages or 1 GB of images return EXPORT_TOO_LARGE with a suggestion to export by section.

Roles: editors, commenters and viewers may export what they can open, in every format; outside reviewers may export PDF only, with a footer naming them and the date. Export stays available in a read_only workspace during a failed payment, and in every plan, because customers must always be able to take their data out. EXP-07 an admin can turn exports off for outside reviewers (CONTRACT-DUNNING-STATES).

Word: EXP-08 export a document as DOCX where open comments become Word comments with author and time, and suggestions become tracked changes the recipient can accept or reject in Word; EXP-09 export a clean copy without comments or suggestions. The HTML archive is removed from 3.5; the per-format table now has PDF, Markdown and DOCX columns (CHANGE-DOCX-EXPORT).

Workspace export: EXP-10 an admin of a Business workspace exports every document (as Markdown and DOCX), every attachment and every comment as one archive with a manifest; EXP-11 the admin gets an email with a link valid for 24 hours when it is done, and every workspace export is recorded in the security events; EXP-12 owners and admins of Team workspaces see the feature with an upgrade note, members never see it (CHANGE-DOCX-EXPORT, CHANGE-WORKSPACE-EXPORT).

steps.notes: Approved. Members never seeing workspace export keeps the page honest (CHANGE-WORKSPACE-EXPORT).

args.summary: Export dialog, job polling, downloads, exports list
args.content:
Web export dialog and downloads, version 1.

Dialog: PDF, Word and Markdown, page size for PDF, and comments and tracked changes or a clean copy for Word. Each click sends its own Idempotency-Key, so a double click creates one job; the dialog polls every second and hands over to a toast after three seconds. A document waiting to sync shows the note and "Export when synced" (CONV-IDEMPOTENCY-KEY).

Downloads: the toast and the notification centre link to the file with "Link valid for 24 hours"; the exports list in settings keeps the last 20 exports. Files are named after the document title as typed, for example "Q3 Plan: Draft #2 / Final?.pdf".

steps.notes: The file names break things: slashes and colons in titles produce files Windows will not save, and two exports of the same document on different days get the same name. Fix the naming everywhere we produce files, not only on the web.
conventions: Exported files are named with one file name pattern on every platform and in the API: <title as an ASCII-safe slug>-<YYYY-MM-DD in UTC>.<ext>, at most 80 characters before the date, for example q3-plan-draft-2-final-2027-03-04.pdf (CONV-EXPORT-FILENAMES).

contracts.spec: Stories are numbered EXP-nn with acceptance checklists that the test plan traces one to one; every result names the story id and the build number (CONV-STORY-AND-BUILD).

Export jobs (CONTRACT-EXPORT-JOBS): POST /v2/exports with {docId, format} and an Idempotency-Key returns 202 and a jobId; GET /v2/exports/{jobId} returns queued, rendering, done or failed, with progress from 0 to 100; a done job has a downloadUrl that expires 24 hours after it was issued and needs no access token. Failures use the {code, message, requestId} body, for example EXPORT_TOO_LARGE (CONTRACT-ERROR-ENVELOPE, CONTRACT-SESSION-TOKENS, CONV-IDEMPOTENCY-KEY).
The same export job endpoints (CONTRACT-EXPORT-JOBS); the apps poll at most every 2 seconds and stop polling in the background, and the export.done push carries the jobId.

The engine runs as a worker image that takes jobs from the export queue, renders from the document's Yjs snapshot, writes the file to the exports bucket and reports progress; a job may use at most 2 GB of memory and 5 minutes (CONTRACT-YJS-SYNC).
Figma frames for the export dialog, progress, the download toast and the finished-export email, using UI kit names.

Exports always render the server snapshot of a document. While the document shows "Waiting to sync", the export dialog says the export will not include those changes and offers to start it once they are synced.

The Markdown writer ships as the @quire/export-markdown package with the same output as the workers; the apps run it on the Yjs document of a pinned document to export Markdown without a connection. PDF and DOCX need the workers (CONTRACT-YJS-SYNC, CHANGE-DOCX-EXPORT).

POST /v2/workspaces/{id}/exports starts a workspace export for admins only (403 FORBIDDEN_ROLE otherwise) and only when the entitlements response lists workspaceExport (Business); the job reports progress like a document export and the archive holds every document as Markdown and DOCX, attachments, comments as JSON and a manifest (CONTRACT-ENTITLEMENTS, CHANGE-DOCX-EXPORT, CHANGE-WORKSPACE-EXPORT).
Every help centre article and API guide section lists the story ids it covers, so QA can check it against the release build.

Workspace exports run on their own queue and workers with 8 GB of memory and no 5-minute limit, so they never delay document exports; a workspace export of 48,000 documents takes about 2 hours (CHANGE-WORKSPACE-EXPORT).

args.content:
Export engine, version 3.

Rendering: a reader turns the document's Yjs snapshot into our block tree, so exports never load the live document on a sync server. PDF is rendered by headless Chromium in the render workers; Markdown writes images next to the file and links them relatively. A 50-page document with 30 images renders to PDF in 11 seconds (CONTRACT-YJS-SYNC).

Jobs: POST /v2/exports takes an Idempotency-Key and returns 202 with a jobId; GET /v2/exports/{jobId} reports queued, rendering, done or failed with progress. Viewers, commenters and editors may export; outside reviewers only PDF with a footer naming them (CONV-IDEMPOTENCY-KEY, CONTRACT-EXPORT-JOBS).

Golden files: the 40 reference documents are rendered to PDF, Markdown and DOCX in CI on every change and compared with the stored golden file; a difference fails the build unless the pull request updates the golden file with a visual diff. DOCX is written directly with the docx library: open comments become Word comments with author and time, suggestions become tracked changes, and table column widths are kept (CHANGE-DOCX-EXPORT, CONV-GOLDEN-FILES).

Workspace export: POST /v2/workspaces/{id}/exports checks the admin role on the server and workspaceExport in the entitlements, then queues one job on the separate workspace queue; the archive holds every document as Markdown and DOCX, attachments, comments as JSON and a manifest with ids, authors and ISO 8601 UTC times. The engine sets every file name from the shared pattern (CONV-ISO8601-UTC, CHANGE-DOCX-EXPORT).

steps.notes: Approved. A separate queue keeps workspace exports from delaying anyone else (CHANGE-WORKSPACE-EXPORT).

args.content:
Render workers and export storage, version 1.

Workers: the render image has Chromium, fonts for 14 scripts and the engine, rebuilt and scanned in CI. Document exports run on 2 to 40 workers scaled on queue depth, with 2 GB and 5 minutes per job; workspace exports have their own queue and workers with 8 GB and no time limit. Each workspace may run 20 jobs at once (CHANGE-WORKSPACE-EXPORT).

Storage: finished files go to a private, encrypted bucket and are deleted after 7 days; download links are signed for 24 hours and carry no access token. Alerts fire when the oldest queued job is older than 2 minutes. At normal volume the pool costs about USD 1,400 a month (CONTRACT-SESSION-TOKENS).

steps.notes: The pool handles a normal day, but the month-end numbers are missing: agencies export six times the normal volume on the last two working days, and the 40-worker ceiling has never been tested against that.
conventions: Every capacity plan is tested against the known peak (month end for exports, the 9:00 reconnects for offline devices) before review, not only against an average day.

steps.text: Quire 3.5 is out: Word export is used by a third of our Business workspaces already. The last release of the year is 3.6, compliance. Enterprise security questionnaires keep asking for three things we do not have: an audit log, admin security policies and a SOC 2 report. For 3.6 I want the audit log, the admin console and everything ready for a SOC 2 Type I audit. Six weeks, same team.

contracts.spec: Stories are numbered CMP-nn with acceptance checklists that the test plan traces one to one; every result names the story id and the build number (CONV-STORY-AND-BUILD).

Audit events (CONTRACT-AUDIT-EVENTS) have the fields {id, at, workspaceId, actor {type, id, email}, action, target {type, id}, ip, userAgent, details}; at is ISO 8601 in UTC and action is a dotted name such as member.role_changed. The store is append-only and keeps events for 400 days. GET /v2/workspaces/{id}/audit-events is for owners and admins only, with filters on action, actor and time and cursor paging (CONV-ISO8601-UTC).

The apps send no audit events themselves; the services record sign-ins, sign-outs and remote wipes. The apps read the workspace policies from GET /v2/workspaces/{id}/policies on launch and on the policies.changed push.
Every infrastructure control produces evidence on a schedule into the evidence bucket, named <control id>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<file>, so the auditor sample can be pulled without asking an engineer.
Figma frames for the admin console and the audit log viewer, using UI kit names; every table works with the keyboard alone.

args.summary: Audit log, admin policies, retention; CMP-01 to CMP-08
args.content:
Compliance requirements, version 1.

Audit log: CMP-01 an owner or admin searches audit events by person, action and time range; CMP-02 exports them as JSON lines; CMP-03 streams them to Splunk, Datadog or Sentinel. Recorded actions include sign-ins and failed sign-ins, two-factor changes, SAML configuration, role changes, billing changes, sharing with outside reviewers, exports and remote wipes of offline devices (CHANGE-SAML-SSO, CHANGE-ADMIN-2FA, CONTRACT-AUDIT-EVENTS).

Policies and retention: CMP-04 set the session length (1 to 30 days) and idle timeout; CMP-05 require two-factor for everyone; CMP-06 restrict sign-up to verified email domains; CMP-07 set retention for trashed documents and removed members' data; CMP-08 a security overview that shows the state of each control a questionnaire asks about (CHANGE-ADMIN-2FA).

steps.notes: Good list. But there is no rule for who can read the audit log, and an admin who changes their own role or removes their own access must not be able to hide it. Spell out the access rules and that the log cannot be edited by anyone, us included.

args.summary: Audit log access rules; append-only for everyone
args.content:
Compliance requirements, version 2.

Audit log: CMP-01 an owner or admin searches audit events by person, action and time range; CMP-02 exports them as JSON lines; CMP-03 streams them to Splunk, Datadog or Sentinel. Recorded actions include sign-ins and failed sign-ins, two-factor changes, SAML configuration, role changes, billing changes, sharing with outside reviewers, exports and remote wipes of offline devices (CHANGE-SAML-SSO, CHANGE-ADMIN-2FA, CONTRACT-AUDIT-EVENTS).

Policies and retention: CMP-04 set the session length (1 to 30 days) and idle timeout; CMP-05 require two-factor for everyone; CMP-06 restrict sign-up to verified email domains; CMP-07 set retention for trashed documents and removed members' data; CMP-08 a security overview that shows the state of each control a questionnaire asks about (CHANGE-ADMIN-2FA).

Access: only owners and admins read the workspace audit log, checked on the server; members read only events about themselves on their account page. The log is append-only for everyone, Quire staff included; an admin who changes their own role or removes their own access is recorded like anyone else, and the event cannot be deleted before its retention ends. CMP-09 a nightly check proves no event was changed or removed.

contracts.spec: Stories are numbered CMP-nn with acceptance checklists that the test plan traces one to one; every result names the story id and the build number (CONV-STORY-AND-BUILD).

Audit events (CONTRACT-AUDIT-EVENTS) have the fields {id, at, workspaceId, actor {type, id, email}, action, target {type, id}, ip, userAgent, details}; at is ISO 8601 in UTC and action is a dotted name such as member.role_changed. args.content:
SOC 2 policies and evidence, version 1 (CHANGE-SOC2-TYPE2).

Policies: information security, access control, change management, incident response, vendor management, business continuity and data retention, each approved by the owner and acknowledged by the team. The control matrix maps 82 controls to the security and availability criteria, each with an owner, a frequency and the evidence it leaves.

steps.notes: The matrix lists "quarterly review of access" without saying what is reviewed, by whom, and what happens to access nobody can justify. The auditor will sample exactly this control first, and our 3.1 admin and SAML rules depend on it (CHANGE-SAML-SSO).
conventions: Every quarter the owner of each system reviews who has production, admin-tool and Stripe access; access nobody can justify is removed within 5 working days, and the review is recorded with the reviewer, the date and the removals (CONV-ACCESS-REVIEW).

args.summary: EU residency CMP-10 and CMP-11; continuous evidence CMP-12
args.content:
Compliance requirements, version 3.

Audit log: CMP-01 an owner or admin searches audit events by person, action and time range; CMP-02 exports them as JSON lines; CMP-03 streams them to Splunk, Datadog or Sentinel. Recorded actions include sign-ins and failed sign-ins, two-factor changes, SAML configuration, role changes, billing changes, sharing with outside reviewers, exports and remote wipes of offline devices (CHANGE-SAML-SSO, CHANGE-ADMIN-2FA, CONTRACT-AUDIT-EVENTS).

Policies and retention: CMP-04 set the session length (1 to 30 days) and idle timeout; CMP-05 require two-factor for everyone; CMP-06 restrict sign-up to verified email domains; CMP-07 set retention for trashed documents and removed members' data; CMP-08 a security overview that shows the state of each control a questionnaire asks about (CHANGE-ADMIN-2FA).

Access: only owners and admins read the workspace audit log, checked on the server; members read only events about themselves on their account page. The log is append-only for everyone, Quire staff included; an admin who changes their own role or removes their own access is recorded like anyone else, and the event cannot be deleted before its retention ends. CMP-09 a nightly check proves no event was changed or removed.

Residency: CMP-10 an EU workspace's documents, attachments, search, exports, audit events, backups and logs are stored and processed only in eu-central-1, and the console shows the region and when the workspace moved; CMP-11 existing EU workspaces move with at most 30 seconds of read-only time. CMP-12 every control in the matrix produces its evidence without manual screenshots from the first day of the Type II window (CONTRACT-AUDIT-EVENTS, CHANGE-EU-RESIDENCY).

contracts.spec: Stories are numbered CMP-nn with acceptance checklists that the test plan traces one to one; every result names the story id and the build number (CONV-STORY-AND-BUILD).

Audit events (CONTRACT-AUDIT-EVENTS) have the fields {id, at, workspaceId, actor {type, id, email}, action, target {type, id}, ip, userAgent, details}; at is ISO 8601 in UTC and action is a dotted name such as member.role_changed. The store is append-only and keeps events for 400 days. GET /v2/workspaces/{id}/audit-events is for owners and admins only, with filters on action, actor and time and cursor paging (CONV-ISO8601-UTC).

The apps send no audit events themselves; the services record sign-ins, sign-outs and remote wipes. The apps read the workspace policies from GET /v2/workspaces/{id}/policies on launch and on the policies.changed push.
Every infrastructure control produces evidence on a schedule into the evidence bucket, named <control id>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<file>, so the auditor sample can be pulled without asking an engineer.
Figma frames for the admin console and the audit log viewer, using UI kit names; every table works with the keyboard alone.
Audit events of Quire staff actions (support access to a workspace, production database access) are recorded like customer events and copied daily to the evidence bucket for the observation window.

Production access, deploys and their reviews, vulnerability scans, backup and restore tests and laptop encryption write evidence automatically every day; the access review and the tabletop exercise write theirs through a form; all of it lands in the evidence bucket under <control id>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/.

Each workspace has a region, us or eu, fixed at creation and readable from GET /v2/workspaces/{id}; every service stores and processes the workspace's data only in that region, including audit events, export files and backups (CONTRACT-AUDIT-EVENTS).
The region and the date of a completed move are part of the workspace response, so the console can show a residency badge; a move in progress is shown as such.

During a region move the sync server closes the workspace's sockets with REGION_MOVING and API writes return 503 with Retry-After: 30; clients keep their unsent edits and reconnect when the gateway routes the workspace to its new region.

args.summary: Audit store, 64 actions, admin API, JSON lines export
args.content:
Audit log service, version 1.

Store: audit events follow the agreed schema and go into an append-only Postgres table written through an insert-only role, partitioned by month, with a hash chain per workspace so a changed or removed row breaks the chain. All services emit through one client library; 64 actions cover identity, two-factor, SAML, roles, billing, sharing, document roles, exports and offline wipes (CHANGE-SAML-SSO, CHANGE-ADMIN-2FA, CONTRACT-AUDIT-EVENTS).

API: GET /v2/workspaces/{id}/audit-events accepts lists and prefixes of actions, actor and ISO 8601 UTC bounds, pages by cursor and is restricted to owners and admins by the server-side role check; members get their own events on the account page. Exports run through the export job queue as JSON lines, named with the shared file name pattern (CONV-ISO8601-UTC, CONV-SERVER-ROLE-CHECK, CONTRACT-EXPORT-JOBS, CONV-EXPORT-FILENAMES).

steps.notes: The store is solid, but the SIEM stream posts events to customer URLs with nothing that proves they came from us, and a retried batch arrives twice. We set the rule for incoming webhooks in 3.2; outgoing ones need the same care.

args.summary: Signed SIEM deliveries with batch ids; policies endpoint
args.content:
Audit log service, version 2.

Store: audit events follow the agreed schema and go into an append-only Postgres table written through an insert-only role, partitioned by month, with a hash chain per workspace so a changed or removed row breaks the chain. All services emit through one client library; 64 actions cover identity, two-factor, SAML, roles, billing, sharing, document roles, exports and offline wipes (CHANGE-SAML-SSO, CHANGE-ADMIN-2FA, CONTRACT-AUDIT-EVENTS).

API: GET /v2/workspaces/{id}/audit-events accepts lists and prefixes of actions, actor and ISO 8601 UTC bounds, pages by cursor and is restricted to owners and admins by the server-side role check; members get their own events on the account page. Exports run through the export job queue as JSON lines, named with the shared file name pattern (CONV-ISO8601-UTC, CONV-SERVER-ROLE-CHECK, CONTRACT-EXPORT-JOBS, CONV-EXPORT-FILENAMES).

SIEM stream: batches of events every 30 seconds are signed with a per-customer secret in a Quire-Signature header (HMAC-SHA256 over the timestamp and body, 5-minute tolerance), the same scheme we verify on incoming webhook signature checks, and carry a batch id so a retried batch can be dropped by the receiver. GET /v2/workspaces/{id}/policies and the policies.changed push serve session and sign-in policies; the identity service refuses refresh tokens older than the session length (CONTRACT-SESSION-TOKENS, CONV-WEBHOOKS-VERIFIED).

args.summary: Production access, central logs, restores, vulnerability deadlines, change management
args.content:
Infrastructure controls, version 1.

Access and logging: production access only through short-lived roles from the identity provider with hardware keys; no long-lived access keys remain. args.content:
SOC 2 policies and evidence, version 2 (CHANGE-SOC2-TYPE2).

Policies: information security, access control, change management, incident response, vendor management, business continuity and data retention, each approved by the owner and acknowledged by the team. The control matrix maps 82 controls to the security and availability criteria, each with an owner, a frequency and the evidence it leaves.

Evidence plan for the Type II window starting on release day: 61 controls leave evidence automatically every day or on every event; 21 are periodic (quarterly or yearly) and write through forms. The audit firm samples from the evidence bucket without asking engineers.

Access review: every quarter the owner of each system (AWS, the admin tool, Stripe, the support tool, the identity provider) reviews who has access; unjustified access is removed within 5 working days and the review is recorded with reviewer, date and removals. System description: architecture, data flows and the two regions, us-east-1 and eu-central-1 for EU workspaces, for the Type II window starting on release day (CHANGE-EU-RESIDENCY).

steps.reply: First version of EU data residency: the Frankfurt region, routing by workspace region, the move procedure and the residency check (CHANGE-EU-RESIDENCY).

args.summary: Frankfurt region, routing by region, workspace moves, residency check (CHANGE-EU-RESIDENCY)
args.content:
EU data residency, version 1.

Region: eu-central-1 is built from the same Terraform modules as us-east-1, with its own Postgres, attachments, search, sync fleet, render workers and export bucket; backups go to eu-central-1 and eu-west-1 only. The gateway routes every request and websocket by the workspace region, not by sticky sessions or the user's location (FAIL-STICKY-SESSIONS, CHANGE-EU-RESIDENCY).

Moves: a workspace is copied, caught up, paused for writes for about 20 seconds while the region switches, and its US copy is deleted after a verification; the 1,140 existing EU workspaces move in nightly batches of 150. A residency check scans every store in every region each night and fails on any EU workspace data outside the EU; replicas and analytics exports stay in the region of their data.

steps.notes: Approved. The nightly residency check is the strongest evidence we have.

args.summary: Admin console with audit viewer, policies, retention, SIEM, overview
args.content:
Web admin console, version 1.

Audit viewer: the table sends its filters to the server (lists and prefixes of actions, actor, time range) and pages by cursor; the side panel shows the full event. Exports go through the export job API. Only owners and admins see the console; the server checks the role on every request (CONTRACT-EXPORT-JOBS).

Settings: session length and idle timeout, two-factor for everyone, SAML enforcement with the break-glass owner, allowed domains, retention with a confirmation that names what will be deleted, SIEM stream settings with a test delivery, the security overview and the residency badge with the region and the date of the move (CHANGE-SAML-SSO, CHANGE-ADMIN-2FA).

steps.notes: The table keeps the last 2,000 events in localStorage to make the back button fast. That puts audit data with IPs and emails in browser storage on whatever computer the admin used, and we learned in 3.4 what localStorage does at its limit. Keep nothing there (FAIL-LOCALSTORAGE-QUOTA).
conventions: Clients keep customer data in browser storage only for pinned offline documents; everything else stays in memory for the open tab.

Web admin console, version 2.

Audit viewer: the table sends its filters to the server (lists and prefixes of actions, actor, time range) and pages by cursor; the side panel shows the full event. Exports go through the export job API. Only owners and admins see the console; the server checks the role on every request (CONTRACT-EXPORT-JOBS).

Storage: the audit viewer keeps events only in memory for the open tab; filters and the cursor live in the URL, so the back button restores the same page with one request instead of a stored copy. steps.reply: First version of the policies in the apps and managed app configuration.

args.summary: Session policies, two-factor for everyone, Intune and Jamf configuration, remote sign-out (CHANGE-ADMIN-2FA)
args.content:
Mobile admin policies and managed devices, version 1.

Policies: the apps read GET /v2/workspaces/{id}/policies on launch and on the policies.changed push; a session that reaches the policy's length or idle timeout ends with a message, and unsynced edits stay on the device until the person signs in again. When two-factor is required for everyone, the app asks for enrolment before opening the workspace (CHANGE-ADMIN-2FA).

Managed devices: Intune and Jamf can set the allowed workspace, turn offline storage off and block screenshots and the app switcher preview; a workspace that requires managed devices refuses to open on an unmanaged one. The remote sign-out push signs the app out within a minute and wipes pinned documents. Tested with a real Intune tenant on both platforms.

steps.notes: Approved. Testing against a real Intune tenant removes the biggest unknown.

args.summary: Plan traced to CMP-01..CMP-12; event coverage; first run
args.content:
Compliance test plan and release pass, version 1.

Plan: CMP-01 to CMP-12 trace to 118 automated cases; the event coverage check performs all 64 actions and looks for each audit event; policy cases run on the web and both apps; residency cases run the residency check after moving three staging workspaces (CONTRACT-AUDIT-EVENTS).

First run, CMP-01 / build 3.6.0-rc1: 113 of 118 pass. Failures: CMP-01 / build 3.6.0-rc1, offline remote wipes are recorded without the device name; CMP-11 / build 3.6.0-rc1, one moved workspace kept its search index in us-east-1; CMP-04 / build 3.6.0-rc1, the idle timeout ends Android sessions 60 seconds early; two flaky SIEM delivery waits.

steps.notes: The coverage check is excellent. But nothing tests the hash chain against tampering or the 400-day retention, and those are the two properties we promise auditors and customers about the log.

args.summary: Hash chain tampering, 400-day retention; release pass on 3.6.0-rc2
args.content:
Compliance test plan and release pass, version 2.

Plan: CMP-01 to CMP-12 trace to 118 automated cases; the event coverage check performs all 64 actions and looks for each audit event; policy cases run on the web and both apps; residency cases run the residency check after moving three staging workspaces (CONTRACT-AUDIT-EVENTS).

First run, CMP-01 / build 3.6.0-rc1: 113 of 118 pass. Failures: CMP-01 / build 3.6.0-rc1, offline remote wipes are recorded without the device name; CMP-11 / build 3.6.0-rc1, one moved workspace kept its search index in us-east-1; CMP-04 / build 3.6.0-rc1, the idle timeout ends Android sessions 60 seconds early; two flaky SIEM delivery waits.

New cases: a row changed and a row deleted directly in a staging copy both break the hash chain and raise the alert within the nightly check; with a test clock past 400 days the oldest events are deleted and the chain restarts from a signed checkpoint; an Enterprise workspace with a 3-year setting keeps them.

Release pass on build 3.6.0-rc2: 124 of 124 automated cases pass, including CMP-01 / build 3.6.0-rc1, CMP-11 / build 3.6.0-rc1 (the search index now moves with the workspace) and CMP-04 / build 3.6.0-rc1, now fixed. Known issue: CMP-03 / build 3.6.0-rc2, the Sentinel test delivery shows success before Sentinel confirms it.

steps.notes: Approved for release. The Type II window starts with this build.

steps.text: Quire 3.6 ships on Monday and the SOC 2 observation window starts the same day. Six releases in one year with the same team: accounts, billing, collaboration, offline, export and compliance. Thank you all (CHANGE-SOC2-TYPE2).
